chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The divorce of the Sunnah is: when the woman becomes pure (from menstruation), let him divorce her once in that state, without (having had) sexual intercourse (with her since her purification), keeping witnesses upon her divorce. So when he intends to revert to her, he should keep witnesses upon the return.

key_terms.الْمُرَاجَعَةِ: The return/revocation — ruju', the husband's right to revoke a revocable divorce and reinstate the marriage, also requiring witnesses
key_terms.جِمَاعٍ: Sexual intercourse — the divorce must occur in a period of purity during which the husband has not had intercourse with the wife
key_terms.طَلَاقُ السُّنَّةِ: Divorce of the Sunnah — the proper, legally valid form of divorce conducted in accordance with prophetic practice
key_terms.طَهُرَتِ: She becomes pure — refers to the end of the menstrual period (hayd), meaning the wife has entered a state of ritual purity (tuhr)
key_terms.يُشْهِدُ: Keeping witnesses — the requirement to have witnesses present at the time of pronouncing the divorce

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a valid divorce of the Sunnah (talaq al-sunnah) according to Imam al-Baqir in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) defines the requirements for a divorce valid according to the Sunnah (talaq al-sunnah). The ruling establishes three conditions: the divorce must occur during the wife's state of purity (tuhr), without prior sexual intercourse in that state, and must be witnessed. The same requirement for witnesses applies to any revocation of the divorce (ruju'). In classical Islamic jurisprudence, a divorce performed during menstruation or during a period of purity after intercourse is considered a 'bid'ah divorce' — one that diverges from the Sunnah and is considered irregular or invalid according to Shia fiqh.
